backlog.spec: Ramp Muon's momentum linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to the current value of 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold it at 0.95. Keep everything else unchanged. Implement by computing the momentum each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param groups before the update.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations in the Muon update from 5 to 3. This makes each optimizer step cheaper, so more steps fit in the 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients as they are unless the code requires a change for fewer iterations. Keep the rest of the optimizer unchanged.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: Scale each matrix parameter's Muon update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so tall and wide matrices get comparable effective step sizes. Keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 and the rest of the update unchanged. Apply the scale to the orthogonalized update before it is applied to the weight.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon learning-rate scaling

backlog.spec: Add decoupled weight decay of 0.01 (scaled by the current LR multiplier) to the AdamW groups for the embedding, lm_head and per-layer scalar parameters. Currently only the Muon matrices get weight decay. Do not change learning rates or betas.
backlog.title: Small weight decay on Adam-managed parameters

backlog.spec: Set the AdamW epsilon to 1e-10 for all Adam-managed parameter groups instead of the default 1e-8. Small gradients on the embeddings and scalars then get proportionally larger normalized updates. No other optimizer changes.
backlog.title: Lower Adam epsilon for bf16-friendly updates

backlog.spec: Scale the learning rate of the hidden-size-dependent Adam groups (lm_head and any model-dim scalars) by 1/sqrt(model_dim / 256), where model_dim is the actual width from ASPECT_RATIO times DEPTH. Leave the embedding and Muon learning rates unchanged. Log the resulting learning rates once at startup.
backlog.title: Width-scaled Adam learning rates

backlog.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO (0.5) of the time budget. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups. Keep WARMUP_RATIO at 0.0.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the last 70% of the 300 s budget. Keep the linear shape and all other hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown fraction

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so the learning rate ramps linearly from 0 to its peak over the first 3% of the time budget, then holds until the warmdown begins. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5. Make sure the warmup multiplier applies to all parameter groups including Muon.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup before the plateau

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the warmdown ends at 10% of the peak learning rate rather than zero. Keep all other schedule settings unchanged. This is a single-constant change plus a check that the schedule formula uses FINAL_LR_FRAC.
backlog.title: Non-zero final learning rate

backlog.spec: Hold the Muon matrix learning rate constant at its peak for the first 60% of the time budget and then decay it linearly to 0.1 times peak at the end. Keep the Adam group schedules on the original linear warmdown. This lets the matrix weights keep moving longer while the embeddings settle.
backlog.title: Muon learning rate decoupled from warmdown

backlog.spec: Add a learned value residual: in each attention layer after the first, mix the layer's value projection with the first layer's value vectors using a per-layer learned scalar initialized to 0.5. Keep the rest of the attention block unchanged. This adds only a few parameters.
backlog.title: Value residual from the first layer

backlog.spec: Apply logit soft-capping before the cross-entropy loss: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). This bounds extreme logits and can stabilize training at the high embedding learning rate. Apply it only in the training and evaluation forward paths that compute logits from the lm_head, without changing the evaluation code path structure.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation with squared ReLU: relu(x) squared, in place of the current activation. Keep the MLP width and the projection shapes unchanged. This is a one-line change in the MLP forward.
backlog.title: Squared ReLU MLP activation

backlog.spec: Use grouped-query attention with the number of key/value heads set to one quarter of the query heads (minimum 1). Keep the number of query heads and head dimension unchanged. The smaller KV projections reduce parameters and memory traffic, which allows more steps in the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with fewer KV heads

backlog.spec: Increase the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000. Keep the head dimension and all other attention settings unchanged. This gives longer-wavelength position signals that may help the sliding-window layers.
backlog.title: RoPE base frequency increase

backlog.spec: Keep the SSSL sliding-window pattern but make every layer full-context attention when it is the last layer of the model. Equivalently, ensure the final layer always uses the L window regardless of the pattern string. Keep the other layers unchanged.
backlog.title: Full attention on the final layer only

backlog.spec: Before each transformer block, mix the running residual with the original token embedding x0 using a learned per-layer pair of scalars (a_i * x + b_i * x0), initialized to a_i=1 and b_i=0. Keep the block internals unchanged. This is a cheap way to keep token identity available in deep layers.
backlog.title: Per-layer mixing with the input embedding

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block to compute attention and the MLP from the same normalized input and add both outputs to the residual, instead of applying them sequentially. Keep the widths and normalization unchanged. This reduces the sequential depth per step and may speed up each step.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP blocks

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention block and each MLP block to exactly zero so every block starts as an identity map. Keep all other initializations unchanged. Confirm that the gradients still flow to the zero-initialized projections on the first step.
backlog.title: Zero-initialized residual output projections

backlog.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 and adjust the gradient accumulation so the micro-batch count halves. This gives twice as many optimizer updates within the 300 s budget at the cost of gradient noise.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch size for more steps

backlog.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE of 2**17 tokens for the first 25% of the time budget, then increase it to 2**19 for the rest. Implement the increase by changing the gradient accumulation count between steps. Keep the learning rates unchanged.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp during training

backlog.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 tokens per optimizer step by doubling gradient accumulation. Keep all learning rates unchanged. This tests whether the gradient quality gain outweighs the loss of optimizer steps inside the fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Larger total batch size with same learning rates

backlog.spec: Add a z-loss penalty of 1e-4 times the mean squared log-sum-exp of the logits to the training loss. This keeps the output normalizer near zero and stabilizes the lm_head. Apply it only to the training loss, not to the reported validation metric.
backlog.title: Z-loss regularization on logits

backlog.spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05 for the Muon matrix parameters. Keep the Adam groups unchanged. Lower decay lets the matrices fit the short 300 s run faster.
backlog.title: Lower Muon weight decay

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step. Use the EMA weights for the final model that is evaluated, while training continues on the raw weights. Keep the evaluation call and summary printing unchanged; only swap the weights used for the forward pass before the evaluation call.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: During the last 20% of the time budget, accumulate a uniform average of the model parameters after each optimizer step. Load the averaged parameters before the final evaluation. This smooths the noisy end of the warmdown without changing the training loop.
backlog.title: Averaging of late checkpoints

backlog.spec: For the first 30% of the time budget, train on the first half of each sequence (half the context length), then switch to full context length for the rest of the run. Keep the batch token count the same by adjusting the number of sequences per micro-batch. Keep the sliding-window pattern unchanged.
backlog.title: Sequence length warmup

backlog.spec: Add a second embedding table indexed by a hash of the previous token and the current token, with a few thousand buckets and model width output. Add its output to the token embedding before the first block. Initialize it to zero so the baseline is unchanged at the start of training.
backlog.title: Bigram hash embedding at the input

backlog.spec: Compute the lm_head projection and cross-entropy in float32 while keeping the rest of the model in bf16 autocast. This removes precision loss in the logits that can limit val_bpb at the end of training. Keep the evaluation path unchanged.
backlog.title: Z-loss-free but use bf16 for logits only

backlog.spec: In the attention module, apply RMSNorm (no learned gain, or a per-head learned gain initialized to 1) to q and k after the head reshape and before RoPE is applied. Keep the scaled dot-product attention call unchanged. This bounds attention logit growth, which often allows the higher matrix LR to run stably. No other hyperparameters change.
backlog.title: QK-norm on queries and keys

backlog.spec: Share one matrix between the token embedding and the lm_head, removing the separate unembedding parameter and its Adam group. Initialize the shared weight with std about 0.02 and use EMBEDDING_LR for it, dropping UNEMBEDDING_LR from the optimizer setup. Multiply the logits by a fixed 1/sqrt(model_dim) scale if the logits are too large at init. This frees parameters and optimizer state for more layers or width at the same budget.
backlog.title: Tie input embedding and lm_head weights

backlog.spec: Replace the two-matrix ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU block: a fused up-projection to 2 x hidden, split into gate and value halves, output = silu(gate) * value, then a down-projection. Set the hidden width to about 2/3 of the current 4 x model_dim so the parameter count is unchanged. Keep the Muon-managed matrices and the rest of the block as they are.
backlog.title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SL", so half of the layers use full attention and the other half use the half-context window, or try "LLLL" as a variant. Only the window assignment per layer changes; the attention code is untouched. With a 300 s budget, fewer restricted layers may improve the bytes-per-token at this context length. Compare against the incumbent on the same hardware.
backlog.title: Sliding-window pattern with no local layers

backlog.spec: Keep DEPTH layers in the forward pass but make the middle two blocks share one set of weights, so the forward pass runs block A, block B, block B again, then the remaining layers. Parameter count drops by one block while compute per step rises slightly. Per-position residual scalars stay separate for each application. This tests whether recurrent depth beats extra unique parameters under a fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Looped middle block with shared weights

backlog.spec: After the attention output is computed and before the output projection, multiply each head's output by a sigmoid gate computed from the block input through a small linear layer of shape model_dim to n_heads, initialized so the gate starts near 1 (bias about +2). The gate projection is a matrix parameter and joins the Muon group. This lets each layer suppress uninformative heads at small parameter cost.
backlog.title: Sigmoid-gated attention output per head

backlog.spec: Before each optimizer step, compute the global L2 norm of all parameter gradients and rescale them so the norm is at most 1.0, using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ on the model parameters. Leave the optimizer hyperparameters unchanged. This guards against loss spikes at the high peak learning rates, which could otherwise waste steps in a short run.
backlog.title: Global gradient-norm clipping

backlog.spec: Give each transformer block's Adam-managed scalar parameters a learning rate that scales geometrically with depth, lr_l = SCALAR_LR * 0.85^(DEPTH-1-l), so the top layers learn fastest and the bottom layers slowest. Apply the same schedule multiplier as the existing warmdown. Muon groups and the embedding groups keep their current learning rates. This is a small, self-contained change to parameter group construction.
backlog.title: Layer-wise learning-rate decay for Adam groups

backlog.spec: During training only, replace a random 5% of the input token ids with uniformly sampled vocabulary ids before the embedding lookup, while keeping the original tokens as the prediction targets. Evaluation and the harness path use the unmodified inputs. The mask is drawn per position using torch.rand with the existing generator, so no seed lines change. This reduces over-reliance on exact local context in a short run.
backlog.title: Input token corruption as a light regularizer

backlog.spec: During training, for each transformer block, randomly skip the attention and MLP residual branches per sample with probability p_l = 0.1 * l / (DEPTH-1), rescaling the surviving branch by 1/(1-p_l) so expectations match. Keep the full model at evaluation. Use a single per-layer Bernoulli draw per batch element. This acts as a depth regularizer; it is most useful if the model is compute-bound rather than data-bound at this budget.
backlog.title: Stochastic residual dropping with depth ramp

backlog.spec: In the Muon orthogonalization routine, replace the fixed quintic Newton-Schulz coefficients (a, b, c) with a per-iteration schedule of polynomial coefficients (the Polar Express set: one distinct (a, b, c) triple for each of the 5 iterations, each tuned to push singular values toward 1 faster near the start of the iteration). Keep the iteration count at 5, keep the bf16 cast, the spectral normalization of the input, and the momentum and weight-decay logic unchanged. Only the coefficient constants and the loop that applies them change, so the diff is a few lines.
backlog.title: Polar Express Newton-Schulz coefficients

backlog.spec: Keep a second copy of all trainable parameters as slow weights, initialized from the starting weights. Run the existing optimizers as usual for k=5 fast steps. Then update slow = slow + alpha * (fast - slow) with alpha=0.5, and copy slow back into the live parameters. Use the slow weights (not the fast ones) for the final validation and for any checkpoint evaluation, so the evaluation call itself stays untouched. Do not change learning rates or the schedule. Only the training loop and a small helper function are added.
backlog.title: Lookahead slow-weight wrapper

backlog.spec: Treat the transformer as an encoder-decoder with symmetric skips. Store the residual stream output of each of the first DEPTH/2 blocks. In the second half, before block i (counting from the middle), add the stored activation from the mirrored encoder block through a learnable per-channel scale initialized to zero. This is a residual-only addition with no new attention or MLP parameters beyond the scales. Keep the existing per-layer scalars and the lm_head path unchanged.
backlog.title: U-Net style long skip connections

backlog.spec: Add one extra lightweight linear head that predicts the token two positions ahead from the final hidden state, sharing the existing embedding matrix as its output projection. Its cross-entropy loss, weighted 0.3, is added to the standard next-token loss during training only. Evaluation and the final val_bpb path use only the original next-token head, so the metric stays comparable. The aux head is not counted as a separate learnable matrix in the optimizer groups beyond the existing embedding group.
backlog.title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head

backlog.spec: In each attention layer, split the query and key projections into two halves per head. Compute two softmax attention maps A1 and A2 from the two query/key halves, and output (A1 - lambda * A2) applied to V, where lambda is a learnable scalar per layer initialized to 0.5 and clamped to [0, 1]. Keep the head count and total projection width so the parameter count stays the same, and keep the sliding-window masks identical. Use the existing scaled dot product attention call twice, once per map, or a single call with the combined mask.
backlog.title: Differential attention

backlog.spec: Apply rotary position embedding only to the first half of each attention head's query and key dimensions, leaving the second half position-free. This lets some channels carry content-only matching across long distances while the rest keep positional structure. Keep the RoPE base frequency and the QK scaling unchanged. The change is a slice in the function that applies rotary embedding, plus concatenation of the unrotated half back before attention.
backlog.title: Partial rotary embedding on half the head dimensions

backlog.spec: Compute the per-token cross-entropy as usual, then in each optimizer step keep only the top 70 percent of tokens by loss value in the batch and average the loss over those tokens alone (detached mask, so no gradient flows through the selection). Scale the mean back so the gradient magnitude matches the unmasked version. Evaluation uses the unmodified loss. This focuses the short training budget on tokens the model currently gets wrong and is a single change to the loss reduction line.
backlog.title: Hard-token loss emphasis

backlog.spec: Apply dropout with probability 0.1 to the attention output and the MLP output of every block, with the rate linearly decaying from 0.1 to 0 over the first 50 percent of the time budget and held at 0 afterward. Dropout is disabled in eval mode, so the metric path is unchanged. The decay ensures the model is not regularized in the final low-LR phase where the model is underfitting. Only the forward pass of the block and a rate variable updated in the training loop change.
backlog.title: Light attention and MLP dropout in the first half of training

backlog.spec: Give each attention layer a learnable scalar temperature s initialized to 1.0, and multiply the attention logits by s times the usual 1/sqrt(head_dim) scale before the softmax. Place s in the Adam-managed scalar group with the existing per-layer scalars so it uses SCALAR_LR and no weight decay. Keep QK normalization and sliding-window masks unchanged. This lets each layer adjust its sharpness of attention independently and adds only one parameter per layer.
backlog.title: Learnable per-layer attention temperature

backlog.spec: Add a learnable bias vector of size vocab to the lm_head output, initialized to the log of the empirical unigram token frequency measured from the first 100 training batches (computed once at startup from the training batches already loaded, with add-one smoothing). The bias is trained with the Adam unembedding group at UNEMBEDDING_LR and receives no weight decay. This removes the early-training cost of learning the marginal token distribution, which matters in a 300 second run. Do not alter the evaluation call or reference prepare.py internals.
backlog.title: Unigram log-prior initialization of the output bias
